reply: Good question, and the difference matters for every problem after this one. An outcome is a single result of the experiment: one face of a die landing up, one sequence of heads and tails, one section of a spinner. A sample space lists all possible outcomes, every single one, each written once. An event is a set of outcomes, which means a group of them chosen from the sample space because they share something you care about, such as every face showing an even number. An event can contain one outcome, several, or even all of them, and that is the key difference: an outcome is one entry on the list, while an event is a collection of entries. So when a problem gives you a count of favorable outcomes, it is telling you the size of the event, and the total count is the size of the sample space. Keep the two sizes separate in your head, and comparing them becomes routine. With that in mind, go back to the dice problem and decide which count is which.
